# Environment annotations — every (name, verb) pair snug has something to say
# about, and the exact text it says. Regenerate with:
#   go test ./internal/policy -update
#
# NONE OF THESE IS A REFUSAL. Every pair below is ACCEPTED — a profile's author
# is a human on the trusted side of snug's boundary, and snug has only
# allowlists. What the table buys is that the row says what the tool will DO,
# on --dry-run and on `snug profile show`. A name missing from this file hands
# over its value with nothing said about it.
#
# Only pairs a profile can actually WRITE are listed: a verb the variable's
# TYPE refuses (environ.merge on a scalar, environ.sanitise on MANPATH) can
# never reach a screen, and a type refusal is snug declining an operation
# rather than denying anyone anything. See internal/policy/testdata/
# refusals.txt for those.

## exact names

ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL       set       ← every request the agent makes, conversation included, goes to this endpoint instead of Anthropic's (documented, not measured on this host)
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL       inherit   ← every request the agent makes, conversation included, goes to this endpoint instead of Anthropic's (documented, not measured on this host)
BASH_ENV                 set       ← every non-interactive bash SOURCES this file at startup; the value must be an absolute path, and one this profile does not grant names a file the sandbox will not have
BASH_ENV                 inherit   ← every non-interactive bash SOURCES this file at startup, and the file is chosen on the host, outside any profile
CARGO_HOME               set       ← the config.toml under this path names a program cargo runs — build.rustc-wrapper ran in place of rustc, as the sandbox's own uid (measured, cargo 1.97.1)
CARGO_HOME               inherit   ← taking the host's value points cargo back at the host's config, which is the file "generate, don't bind" exists to avoid; `set` it to a path a profile authored
CC                       set       ← make's implicit rules run this as the compiler (measured)
CC                       inherit   ← make's implicit rules run this as the compiler (measured)
CLASSPATH                merge     ← the JVM's application class loader searches these in order, so an application class here shadows one later on the path; platform/JDK classes are not shadowed, and `java -cp` and `java -jar` ignore this variable outright (measured, temurin 21, in a container — no JVM on this host)
CLASSPATH                prepend   ← the JVM's application class loader searches these in order, so an application class here shadows one later on the path; platform/JDK classes are not shadowed, and `java -cp` and `java -jar` ignore this variable outright (measured, temurin 21, in a container — no JVM on this host)
CLASSPATH                sanitise  ← the JVM's application class loader searches these in order, so an application class here shadows one later on the path; platform/JDK classes are not shadowed, and `java -cp` and `java -jar` ignore this variable outright (measured, temurin 21, in a container — no JVM on this host)
DOCKER_CONFIG            set       ← credsStore in this directory's config.json is a program docker executes, and it runs before docker reaches a daemon (measured, docker 29.4)
DOCKER_CONFIG            inherit   ← taking the host's value points docker back at the host's config, credentials included; `set` it to a path a profile authored
EDITOR                   set       ← the value is a command; git runs it for a commit message via GIT_EDITOR -> core.editor -> VISUAL -> EDITOR (measured)
EDITOR                   inherit   ← the value is a command; git runs it for a commit message via GIT_EDITOR -> core.editor -> VISUAL -> EDITOR (measured)
ENV                      set       ← every non-interactive sh SOURCES this file at startup; the value must be an absolute path, and one this profile does not grant names a file the sandbox will not have
ENV                      inherit   ← every non-interactive sh SOURCES this file at startup, and the file is chosen on the host, outside any profile

## what the VALUE is, and therefore whether a relative one is refused
#
# shape:    the annotation's own column (path / program / opaque), '-' for a
#           name with no annotation.
# roster:   what envTypes says, which is what the grant-COUPLING rule reads.
# relative: valueIsAPath — REFUSED means `environ.set NAME = "x"` cannot be
#           written, because a relative path means whatever is in the directory
#           the payload was last in, which inside snug is --chdir <target>.

ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL       opaque    -            accepted
BASH_ENV                 path      pathNoGrant  REFUSED
CARGO_HOME               path      path         REFUSED
CC                       program   (no row)     accepted
CDPATH                   -         path         REFUSED
CLASSPATH                path      path         REFUSED
DOCKER_CONFIG            path      path         REFUSED
EDITOR                   program   -            accepted
ENV                      path      pathNoGrant  REFUSED
GCONV_PATH               path      (no row)     REFUSED
GETCONF_DIR              path      (no row)     REFUSED
GH_CONFIG_DIR            -         (no row)     REFUSED
GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL       opaque    (no row)     accepted
GIT_ASKPASS              program   (no row)     accepted
GIT_COMMON_DIR           path      (no row)     REFUSED
GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL        -         (no row)     REFUSED
GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM        path      (no row)     REFUSED
GIT_DIR                  path      (no row)     REFUSED
